blocks.task_summary: Show by implicit differentiation that (1 + ln(xy)) dy/dx + (1 + y/x) = 0 for the curve y = x − xy ln(xy), x > 0, y > 0.
method_path: Differentiate y = x − xy ln(xy) implicitly, applying product rule and chain rule to xy ln(xy)
Collect all dy/dx terms on one side
Algebraically rearrange to obtain (1 + ln(xy)) dy/dx + (1 + y/x) = 0
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: rewrite as y/x = 1 − ln(xy) − y ln(xy) then differentiate implicitly
Method 3: treat (x ln(xy)) and y as separate factors via product rule
Method 4: substitute w = xy, differentiate w.r.t. x using dy/dx = dw/dx relation, then simplify

evidence.basis: M1: attempts to differentiate implicitly including at least one application of the product rule
A1: correct differentiation and simplification to the required form
A1: final line (1+ln(xy))(dy/dx)+(1+y/x)=1 leading to AG

blocks.task_summary: Hence find the equation of the tangent to C at the point where x = 1.
method_path: Substitute x = 1 into y = x − xy ln(xy) to obtain y = 1 − y ln y and solve y = 1
Substitute x = 1, y = 1 into the differentiated result (1 + ln(xy)) dy/dx + (1 + y/x) = 0
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: substitute x = 1 into the derivative relation first, then use y = 1 − y ln y to determine dy/dx = 0, then find y = 1 and tangent y = 1

evidence.basis: M1: substitutes x = 1 into y = x − xy ln(xy)
A1: y = 1 − y ln y ⇒ y = 1
M1: substitutes x = 1 and their non-zero value of y into the derivative expression
A1: equation of the tangent is y = 1
